claims.text: The local row and Bulbapedia place the Pokemon Card GB Official Guidebook insert route on January 28, 1999.
Bulbapedia identifies the Pokemon Card GB Official Guidebook as a strategy guide for the Game Boy Color Pokemon Trading Card Game, with an overview of TCG rules and a Venusaur promo included.

Bulbapedia says the Official Guidebook was authored by Shusuke Motomiya and One Up under the supervision of Creatures, Inc.; this makes the route a guidebook/editorial apparatus as much as a card object.
The local source slice models one source-pinned card row for this route: Venusaur source index 082.
Bulbapedia's Venusaur page says the card was created for Pokemon Trading Card Game for Game Boy Color and later released physically, including Japanese guidebook and English Wizards Promo contexts.
PokeBoon and Bulbapedia's Venusaur page credit the guidebook/Venusaur promo art to Ken Sugimori.
As judged collector texture, Venusaur matters because it shows a different Game Boy contact path from Dragonite: not the game pack-in, but the guidebook that helped players read and master the game.

Agents should keep this guidebook Venusaur route separate from Pokemon Card GB Dragonite, Fossil/Base Venusaur memories, Japanese CD promo Venusaur, Intro Pack / Intro Deck Venusaur, English Wizards Promo 13, and later Venusaur V/VMAX products.

The legible target is Venusaur plus Pokemon Card GB Official Guidebook route plus GB-symbol/guidebook evidence; catalog facts do not prove possession, authenticity, condition, price, complete guidebook packaging, or spendability.

narrative.human_title: Venusaur in the book that taught the Game Boy cards
narrative.why_it_matters: Pokemon Card GB Venusaur is wonderful because it makes a strategy guide feel like part of the card game machine. Dragonite says the cartridge can hand you a card; Venusaur says the book beside the cartridge can do it too. That is a different kind of assembly: Motomiya, One Up, Creatures supervision, Game Boy rules, Sugimori's starter-line authority, and a promo tucked into the learning apparatus. It is not just a famous dinosaur-plant. It is Pokemon teaching people how to read itself.

narrative.why_it_matters: This Venusaur has that old Sugimori steadiness: not flashy, not coy, just the big final starter standing there like a piece of the franchise's foundation. The route gives it the charm. It comes through the Official Guidebook, so the card feels attached to learning: rules, deck play, Game Boy menus, and the slow pleasure of figuring the system out. For an agent, the beauty and the danger are the same. Venusaur is famous enough to blur; the guidebook route has to stay sharp.
